role: Format C — the reversal. Lay the theory out honestly, in its own words, then show what the record actually says. The hook is the theory; the payoff is the answer.
editorial_note: Selena Gomez is alive. Every claim in the first half is attributed to the theory, never stated as fact — 'the internet has decided', 'people pulled up'. Every claim in the second half is on the public record: the lupus diagnosis (2015), the kidney transplant from Francia Raisa (September 2017), her own Instagram announcement, and the press coverage that called the Epstein screenshot unverified. The film never leaves the viewer holding the theory.
voice_note: Running sentences, hedges left in, no chains of one-word fragments. The first half is told the way a friend repeats something they read; the turn at L05 is flat and unhurried, not triumphant.

lines.en: The internet has decided that Selena Gomez died in 2017, and that whoever you've watched since is a replacement.
lines.vo_direction: Level, almost bored. Reporting what other people believe.

lines.en: It starts with a screenshot of an email dated July 2017: he has decided on Selena Gomez.
lines.vo_direction: Read the quote plainly, no menace.

lines.en: Weeks later she disappeared, and came back with a face that didn't match.
People pulled up photos from 2010 and started measuring her beauty mark.
That July she was already in hospital, and in September her friend Francia Raisa gave her a kidney.
lines.vo_direction: Warmer. This is the real story.

lines.en: She has lupus, and the steroid that keeps it quiet swells your face.
The hospital photo used as proof is one she posted herself.
And the screenshot has never been verified — it even spells decided wrong.
She wasn't replaced, she was ill and then she wasn't, and she's still posting.
